legalese_flags: Highly specific weapon-type inclusions: only airstrikes (bombs, air-to-surface missiles, air-launched drones) and surface-to-surface missiles/one-way attack drones qualify
Explicit exclusions: cyber ops, naval gunfire, artillery, ground incursions, small-arms fire, short-range loitering munitions, FPV drones, ATGMs, surface-to-air missiles
Interception/debris rule: intercepted munitions or debris landing on Iran do not qualify
Geographic precision requirement: strike must be clearly attributable to internationally recognized Iranian territory
Specific European country list provided — excludes Russia, Turkey, and other states sometimes considered European
3-day attribution window with potential deadline extension for conflicting reports
No-declaration or announcement alone qualifies; executed kinetic action required
Deadline timezone specified as CEST 11:59 PM, but market horizon stated as 2026-12-31 while title says December 31 without year — minor ambiguity on year
scholar.rationale: The contract is a subset of engine event A because it restricts qualifying actions to specific strike modalities (airstrikes and surface-to-surface missiles) by a defined list of European states against Iran, excluding many other forms of kinetic military action (naval gunfire, ground incursions, cyber, etc.) that would count under the broader conflict-onset definition.

clergy.rationale: Method_specific burden (airstrike or surface-to-surface missile only, excluding cyber/naval/ground) drives P(B|A) well below 1.0 since European conflict onset could take many non-qualifying forms; WarCosts=-1.0 (very high cost of war) and PatronDeterrence=1.5 (Iran has meaningful patron backing from Russia/China) both suppress probability toward the low end of the range, while WinProbability=0.6 (modest European capability edge) and AudienceCosts=1.2 provide some upward pressure but are insufficient to overcome the structural cost barriers; no European state has conducted a direct airstrike on Iranian territory in modern history, making P(B|¬A) negligible.

glass.rationale: While a European airstrike on Iran would be major news reported immediately by wire services, the highly specific weapon-type inclusions/exclusions, interception/debris rules, 3-day attribution window, and year ambiguity create substantial resolution risk that Polymarket admins could plausibly rule incorrectly or dispute even if a qualifying event occurs.

scholar.win_condition_summary: Iran must conduct an airstrike or surface-to-surface/one-way-attack-drone strike explicitly claimed by Iran or confirmed to originate from Iranian territory, directed at one of 21 named Arab countries, before September 30, 2026.
legalese_flags: Restricted to airstrikes and surface-to-surface missile/drone strikes only — excludes ground incursions, naval gunfire, cyber, small arms, artillery, rocket artillery, short-range loitering munitions, FPV drones, ATGMs
Proxy forces (Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) explicitly excluded — must be Iranian forces with Iranian claim or confirmed Iranian-territory origin
Surface-to-air missile strikes explicitly excluded
Interception of munitions does not negate qualification, but strike must be a qualifying type
Action must be directed at terrestrial territory or internal waters of a qualifying Arab country
Named list of 21 qualifying Arab countries — excludes non-Arab states
3-day conflict resolution window for disputed attribution that may extend past deadline
Arabia Standard Time (AST) governs deadline
Only actions between market creation and listed date qualify
scholar.rationale: The contract covers a specific subset of conflict onset — only direct Iranian kinetic strikes (airstrikes or surface-to-surface missiles/drones) explicitly excluding proxies, ground incursions, cyber, and many other forms of military action that would qualify as conflict onset under the engine's broader definition.

clergy.rationale: Method_specific burden (airstrike or surface-to-surface/drone only, not ground/naval/proxy/cyber) with proxy exclusion significantly reduces P(B|A) from a broad baseline since Iran's most common conflict actions against Arab states historically route through proxies (Houthis, Hezbollah) or gray-zone methods; WarCosts = -0.8 (very high cost of war) and PatronDeterrence = 1.5 (strong external patron coverage for Gulf Arab states, e.g. US umbrella) both suppress the probability of direct Iranian kinetic action against Arab territory, pushing toward the lower end of the range, while WinProbability = 0.3 (modest Iranian capability advantage) and AudienceCosts = 1.5 offer slight upward pressure but are dominated by the structural deterrence signals; P(B|¬A) reflects the low but non-zero historical rate of Iran launching direct attributed strikes into Arab-state territory (as distinct from proxy operations), roughly consistent with Iran's April 2024 direct strike precedent but still rare on a monthly basis.

glass.rationale: While a major Iranian strike would be widely reported, the highly specific exclusions (proxy forces, naval gunfire, rocket artillery, cyber, SAMs) create significant threshold ambiguity requiring precise attribution and weapon-type confirmation that open-source reporting may not always provide, and Polymarket admin discretion over disputed cases adds substantial resolution risk.
